result.area: O-06 security: insider (technician, manager) and operator threat model, including a home server exposed through Cloudflare Tunnel

hypothesis_ranking.id: H-O6a: a technician can create attendance/location evidence the manager cannot tell apart from a genuine punch
hypothesis_ranking.discriminating_test: With a tech's own PIN-derived JWT, POST /api/attendance/punch from a laptop with workshop lat/lng, accuracy_m=5, is_mock_location=false, device_time=now, and upload any photo to the minted selfie URL. Then check that the board shows status present with no mock/outside/drift/no_selfie flag. Code says it will. The only remaining signal is wifi_match, if the fence has BSSIDs, and that is forgeable too.

hypothesis_ranking.id: H-O6b: a technician can move the cash payable on any job without a manager approving or being alerted
hypothesis_ranking.discriminating_test: As tech t2, POST /api/jobs/{t3's job}/bill/negotiate with amount_paisa=0 after bill_sent_at is set and a payment exists. Expect 200 and bill_status=negotiated. The only trace is a timeline text line naming t2.

hypothesis_ranking.id: H-O6c: a manager can rewrite money history so that only free-text timeline lines remain
hypothesis_ranking.discriminating_test: As a manager: resubmit the completion on a paid, unclosed job with fewer materials, void the payment, log a smaller one. Then query job_material (the old lines are gone), job.bill_original_paisa (overwritten) and job_payment (no voided_by/voided_at). Only job_event text remains, in whole rupees.

hypothesis_ranking.id: H-O6d: whoever operates the DB host can change money rows with nothing detecting it
hypothesis_ranking.discriminating_test: On a restored copy: UPDATE job_payment SET amount_paisa=... (no chain covers it), and rewrite one staff_ledger row and recompute every staff_ledger_chain row_hash with chain.compute_row_hash. GET /api/attendance/ledger/verify then returns ok=true.

hypothesis_ranking.id: H-O6e: Cloudflare Tunnel by itself makes the home box safe to expose
hypothesis_ranking.discriminating_test: List every hostname in the tunnel's ingress config and check which ones sit behind Cloudflare Access. Run `docker ps --format '{{.Ports}}'` for any 0.0.0.0 publish (Docker bypasses ufw, R-03 F16). Run `env | grep FIXFLOW_ENVIRONMENT` in the API container. Any of these being open defeats the tunnel's no-inbound-port property.

hypothesis_ranking.id: H-O6f: a technician on a shared phone can destroy another technician's unsynced job writes
hypothesis_ranking.discriminating_test: On one device: tech A queues a payment on job J and it fails (with prod gone, any 404 does this, S9). Log out, log in as B, open J. Expect A's item to appear under NEEDS ATTENTION with an enabled Discard.

findings.title: Booting the backend on a non-Railway host without FIXFLOW_ENVIRONMENT=production signs JWTs with the public dev secret
findings.claim: The production JWT boot guard only fires when FIXFLOW_ENVIRONMENT=production or RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT is set. A home-server backend started without that variable therefore serves HS256 tokens signed with DEV_JWT_SECRET, a constant committed in the repo, and anyone can mint a manager token.
findings.failing_condition: Self-hosted deploy (no RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT in the env) where FIXFLOW_ENVIRONMENT is unset or not 'production' and FIXFLOW_JWT_SECRET is unset. The API hostname is reachable through the tunnel.
evidence: backend/app/core/config.py:17 — DEV_JWT_SECRET = "dev-insecure-secret-change-me-in-production-32b"
backend/app/core/config.py:151 — jwt_secret: str = DEV_JWT_SECRET
backend/app/core/config.py:160 — environment: str = "dev"
backend/app/core/config.py:221 — return self.environment.lower() == "production" or bool(os.getenv("RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT"))
backend/app/core/config.py:228 — if self.is_production and self.jwt_secret == DEV_JWT_SECRET: raise
findings.impact: Complete authentication bypass from the internet: forged manager tokens give every money, ledger, attendance and media endpoint. The guard was correct on Railway only because Railway injected RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT. The migration removes that crutch silently.
findings.fix_sketch: Fail closed. Refuse to boot with DEV_JWT_SECRET unless FIXFLOW_ENVIRONMENT is explicitly 'dev' AND the database host is localhost/127.0.0.1, or default environment to 'production' and require dev to opt in. Also enforce a minimum jwt_secret length. Add a deep-health check that reports 'dev secret in use'.

findings.title: Any authenticated technician can renegotiate any job's bill to any amount, including after the customer saw or paid it
findings.claim: negotiate_bill checks only that the job is not closed and has a bill. Every authenticated principal can reach it. It does not check the assigned tech, bill_sent_at, existing payments or any lower bound. So a technician can set bill_negotiated_paisa to Rs 0 on another technician's already-sent, already-paid job, and no manager approves or is alerted.
findings.failing_condition: Tech JWT; POST /api/jobs/{any non-closed job with a bill}/bill/negotiate {amount_paisa: 0}, including when job.bill_sent_at is set or a non-voided payment exists.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/router.py:309-323 — negotiate_bill takes principal: CurrentPrincipal, no Depends(require_manager)
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1385-1388 — the only guards are status == 'closed' and bill_original_paisa is None
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1392-1393 — row.bill_negotiated_paisa = amount_paisa; row.bill_status = 'negotiated'
backend/app/features/jobs/schemas.py:146 — amount_paisa: int = Field(..., ge=0) (no upper/lower bound relative to original)
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1612 — the assigned-tech check `if not actor_is_manager and row.assigned_tech_id != actor` exists for other actions but not here
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1176-1195 — the 'bill freeze' covers only completion resubmit, not negotiate
findings.impact: This is the classic cash-skim path. The customer pays the sent figure, the tech records a lower negotiated amount and logs matching cash, and the difference disappears. It also undercuts the CLAUDE.md claim that a bill the customer has seen is frozen. The only trace is a 'Bill negotiated Rs a → Rs b' text line on the job timeline.
findings.fix_sketch: Server-side: a non-manager negotiate requires the caller to be the assigned tech. After bill_sent_at or the first payment, a tech negotiate becomes a pending request that a manager approves. Add a per-shop shop_setting cap on tech discounts (percent or absolute) above which approval is required. Record the negotiate in a bill-revision table with a payload (from, to, actor). Deployed APKs keep working: below the cap it is unchanged; above it they get a 409 the outbox parks with the reason.

findings.title: Payments can be logged by any technician on any job, closed jobs included, and a manager can void a payment on a closed job
findings.claim: log_payment and void_payment check neither job status nor assignment. So a payment row can be added to, or voided on, a job that is already closed. The web UI hides Void on closed jobs, but the API does not refuse it.
findings.failing_condition: Tech JWT: POST /api/jobs/{closed job}/payments → 200 and a new job_payment row. Manager JWT: POST /api/jobs/{closed job}/payments/{id}/void → 200, received total changes after settlement.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/router.py:339-353 — log_payment takes CurrentPrincipal only
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1456-1468 — _load then add_payment with no status or assigned_tech check
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1501-1508 — void_payment loads and flips voided with no closed-job guard
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1155-1156 — contrast: submit_completion refuses a closed job
findings.impact: A settled, closed job's cash can be rewritten after the fact. A manager voiding cash on a closed job is invisible to anyone who trusts 'closed is terminal'. A future Odoo export keyed on closed jobs would export figures that later change.
findings.fix_sketch: Refuse log_payment and void_payment when status == 'closed' (409 with the plain-text '(current status: closed)' suffix the clients already regex). Require the assigned tech or a manager for log_payment. Post-close corrections become an explicit manager 'reopen-for-correction' or reversal record.

findings.title: Any technician can submit the first completion, which generates the bill, on a job assigned to someone else
findings.claim: submit_completion has no assigned-tech check. Any authenticated technician can create the first completion, and so set bill_original_paisa, fuel and labour, on another technician's job. They can also resubmit it freely until a bill send, negotiation or payment freezes it.
findings.failing_condition: Tech t2 POSTs /api/jobs/{job assigned to t3}/completion before t3 does (or before any freeze trigger).
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/router.py:279-295 — CurrentPrincipal; only is_manager is derived from the role
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1153-1159 — closed check, then the freeze only `if completion is not None and not is_manager`
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1269 — completion.submitted_by = actor (recorded, not checked)
findings.impact: Bills can be authored or zeroed by a technician who did not do the work. Labour and fuel attribution in reports is then wrong.
findings.fix_sketch: Require principal.tech_id == row.assigned_tech_id or a manager, matching the existing check at service.py:1612. Test this against the deployed APK's reassignment flow first.

findings.title: A fresh database seeds every account, including the manager, with PIN 1234 and never forces a change
findings.claim: Migrations 0004 and 0012 seed t1–t5 and manager m1 with a PIN hash of the literal '1234', and nothing forces a change at first login. So a home-server database built with `alembic upgrade head` and exposed through the tunnel accepts a manager login with a publicly known PIN until someone changes it.
findings.failing_condition: Fresh DB (W0 unknown: no restorable dump) and the tunnel published before PINs are rotated. POST login as m1 with PIN 1234.
evidence: backend/alembic/versions/0004_create_technicians.py:28 — _DEFAULT_PIN = "1234"
backend/alembic/versions/0004_create_technicians.py:70 — "pin_hash": hash_pin(_DEFAULT_PIN)
backend/alembic/versions/0012_dedicated_manager_account.py:31 — _DEFAULT_PIN = "1234"
Grep of backend/app/features/identity for must_change/pin_changed/default_pin: no match
findings.impact: Full manager takeover without guessing. The per-account lockout (CLAUDE.md) is irrelevant because the first attempt succeeds.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a must_change_pin flag set by the seed and cleared by set_pin, and refuse all non-identity endpoints for a must_change principal. Or seed with a random PIN printed once by a bootstrap script. Add a deep-health 'default PIN still active' warning. W0 checklist: rotate PINs before the tunnel goes up.

findings.title: Nightly DB dumps are unencrypted, stored in the media bucket, and deletable with the same credential the API holds
findings.claim: run_db_backup uploads a plaintext pg_dump (customer PII, cash, staff ledger, PIN hashes) into the single r2_bucket used for media. It uses the same R2 key that also lists and deletes backups. So anyone holding the backend's env, or code execution in the API, can read every dump and delete every backup.
findings.failing_condition: Leak of FIXFLOW_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET (env file on the home box, a container compromise, a backup of the env), or a buggy prune.
evidence: backend/app/core/backup.py:87-96 — pg_dump --format=custom ... no encryption step
backend/app/core/backup.py:122 — store.put_bytes(key, data, 'application/octet-stream')
backend/app/core/backup.py:125-131 — list_keys + store.delete(old) with the same client
backend/app/core/storage.py:148-149 — delete_object on self._bucket
backend/app/core/storage.py:180-188 — one boto3 client with settings.r2_access_key_id/secret and settings.r2_bucket
backend/app/core/config.py:192-202 — 'Dumps land in the media bucket under backup_prefix'
findings.impact: Confidentiality: the whole business dataset leaks in one object read. Availability: the 'separate provider' backup is one credential away from deletion, and that same deletion removes the external anchor chain.py relies on for tail-truncation detection.
findings.fix_sketch: Encrypt before upload with age/gpg to a public key whose private key the owner holds offline. Use a separate backups bucket and a separate token scoped to PutObject only, with no List/Delete. Move retention to a bucket lifecycle rule plus a bucket lock/retention policy (check that R2 supports it) instead of app-side delete. On the home box, also keep a second copy off-box.

findings.title: The staff-ledger hash chain is unkeyed, unanchored and never verified automatically
findings.claim: row_hash is a plain sha256 over a canonical form published in chain.py. Verification runs only when a manager calls GET /ledger/verify, and no web screen or scheduler calls it. So anyone with DB write access can rewrite staff_ledger rows, recompute the whole chain so verify returns ok, or truncate its tail, and nothing raises an alarm.
findings.failing_condition: An operator or attacker with write access to the Postgres database (home-box superuser, the app role, or a restored dump edited and reloaded).
evidence: backend/app/features/attendance/chain.py:20 — row_hash = sha256(version ‖ payload ‖ prev_hash)
backend/app/features/attendance/chain.py:128-132 — compute_row_hash uses hashlib.sha256, no key
backend/app/features/attendance/chain.py:38-44 — 'cannot ... detect truncation of the whole tail ... The external anchor for that is the nightly DB backup'
backend/app/features/attendance/router.py:532-546 — verify is an on-demand manager GET
Grep of backend/app for verify_ledger/verify_chain: only router.py, service.py and chain.py; no scheduler job, and S-04 F36 records no web UI file referencing the staff ledger
findings.impact: The chain detects only clumsy tampering and only if someone remembers to look. Against the home-box operator, the actor this task is about, it gives no protection.
findings.fix_sketch: (1) Schedule a daily verify that writes ok/head_hash to app_event and alerts the owner on failure. (2) Anchor the daily head_hash outside the operator's control: a WhatsApp or email to the owner, or a write-once object in a locked bucket under a different account. (3) Optionally HMAC the chain with a key held outside the DB, for example in an env that only the API process reads. That still does not stop an operator who has both.

findings.title: Customer cash (job_payment) has no tamper evidence, and its void is not attributable to the voided row
findings.claim: job_payment has no voided_by/voided_at and no hash chain. The void's job_event carries neither the payment id nor the amount in its payload. So a direct-DB edit of amount_paisa or voided goes undetected, and when a job has two voids nothing links a void event to the row it voided.
findings.failing_condition: DB write access (operator), or two payments voided on the same job with similar reasons.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/models.py:481-495 — columns id, job_id, client_id, amount_paisa, method, recorded_by, recorded_at, voided, void_reason only
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1507-1515 — payment.voided = True; job_event text 'Payment voided — {reason}' with no payload
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1478-1484 — payment event text 'Payment Rs {amount // 100}' (whole rupees, no payment id, no payload)
findings.impact: The money table most exposed to skimming is less protected than the staff ledger. Forensics can only rebuild 'who voided which payment when' by matching free text, and a future Odoo pakka-khata export cannot prove its inputs were unaltered.
findings.fix_sketch: Add voided_by/voided_at (migration 0047, nullable, backfill none). Emit payment and void events with payload {payment_id, amount_paisa, method}. Generalise chain.py to a money chain covering job_payment create/void and bill revisions, with the same advisory-lock append.

findings.title: A manager's completion override rewrites the bill and deletes the prior material lines, with no snapshot kept
findings.claim: When a manager resubmits a frozen completion, clear_materials deletes the existing job_material rows and bill_original_paisa is overwritten. No reason is required. The only history is a 'Work completed — bill Rs N' text event in whole rupees, so the bill the customer actually saw cannot be reconstructed.
findings.failing_condition: Manager POST /api/jobs/{id}/completion on a job with bill_sent_at set or a non-voided payment, before close.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/router.py:294 — is_manager=principal.role == 'manager'
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1159 — the freeze is skipped when is_manager
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1225 — await self._repo.clear_materials(completion.id)
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1281-1289 — row.bill_original_paisa = original; event text uses original // 100
backend/app/features/jobs/schemas.py:124-136 — CompletionRequest has no reason field
findings.impact: A manager can lower a paid bill, void the cash and log less, and leave only text lines. Disputes with customers ('you charged me X') cannot be settled from data.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an append-only job_bill_revision table (job_id, rev, kind completion|override|negotiate, original_paisa, negotiated_paisa, materials JSONB snapshot, labour/fuel, actor, reason, created_at) written on every change. Require a reason on a manager override.

findings.title: Attendance adjustments take the 'manager_id' audit actor from the request body
findings.claim: create_adjustment records manager_id and created_by from the client-supplied body, not the authenticated principal. So any manager can file a correction attributed to another manager or to a technician id, as long as the FK resolves.
findings.failing_condition: Manager JWT for m1; POST /api/attendance/adjustments with manager_id='t1' (or another manager's id).
evidence: backend/app/features/attendance/schemas.py:484 — manager_id: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=128)
backend/app/features/attendance/router.py:367-371 — create_adjustment(body, service, session) with no principal parameter
backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:580-586 — created_by=body.manager_id; create_adjustment(manager_id=body.manager_id, ...)
backend/app/features/attendance/models.py:356-357 — manager_id FK technician.id (any existing tech id passes)
src/features/attendance/pages/AttendanceTechDetail.jsx:230 — manager_id: user?.tech_id || 'manager'
findings.impact: The audit row meant to answer 'who corrected this attendance day' is caller-asserted, which defeats it as evidence in a pay dispute.
findings.fix_sketch: Inject CurrentManager in the router and pass principal.tech_id. Ignore or reject a body manager_id that differs. Keep the field optional for compatibility.

findings.title: Manager attendance corrections can only lengthen a day, never shorten it
findings.claim: classify_day uses the earliest clock_in and the latest clock_out, and adjustments only append events whose original_event_id is ignored by the derivation. So a manager cannot correct a padded day: an early remote clock-in or a late or forgotten clock-out stays in worked_minutes.
findings.failing_condition: A tech clocks in from home at 07:00 (or via a direct API call) or clocks out at 23:00. The manager files an adjustment clock_in 09:30 / clock_out 18:00 with original_event_id set. worked_minutes is unchanged.
evidence: backend/app/features/attendance/derive.py:116-125 — clock_ins sorted; first_in = clock_ins[0]; last_out = clock_outs[-1]
backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:560-581 — adjustment appends a new manual event; the original is not edited, voided or excluded
backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:582-587 — original_event_id stored only on the audit row
findings.impact: Inflated hours flow into payroll and into the accrued balance that advances are capped against, and the manager's correction, though recorded, does not take effect.
findings.fix_sketch: Make an adjustment with original_event_id supersede that event in derive. Exclude superseded events in _window/classify_day while keeping both rows. That is append-only and needs no schema change beyond reading attendance_adjustment.

findings.title: Mock-location is a client-asserted flag that never affects the verdict, so a direct API punch is indistinguishable from a genuine one
findings.claim: is_mock_location, lat/lng, accuracy_m, device_time and wifi_bssid all come from the request body, and the server's inside verdict ignores is_mock. So a technician calling the API with their own token, or a fake-GPS app that clears the mocked bit, gets status 'present' with no flag. A flagged mock punch inside the fence still counts as present with full worked minutes.
findings.failing_condition: Tech POSTs /api/attendance/punch with workshop coordinates, accuracy_m=5, is_mock_location=false. Or a mocked fix (pos.mocked=true) inside the fence, which then shows only an icon.
evidence: backend/app/features/attendance/schemas.py:36-45 — tech_id, device_time, lat, accuracy_m, is_mock_location: bool = False, wifi_bssid all from body
backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:332-338 — _evaluate_geofence(lat, lng, accuracy_m, wifi_bssid): is_mock not an input
backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:973-1007 — inside depends only on distance/accuracy
backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:1196 — mock=any(e.is_mock_location ...) feeds only DayFlags
technician-app/src/features/attendance/location.ts:39 — is_mock_location: pos.mocked ?? false
technician-app/src/features/jobs/arrivalGate.ts:73-77,93-104 — GateFix has no mock field; target null always allows
findings.impact: What the manager sees for an honest-looking spoof: nothing. For a flagged spoof: a small icon on the board row and payroll CSV flag_mock_gps (S-03 F7), while the status, hours and pay stay unaffected. Flag-never-block is an owner decision, but the flag is only as strong as the client's honesty.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep flag-never-block, but (a) demote a mock first clock-in's inside verdict to None so the status is not 'present by fence', (b) add an 'uncorroborated' day flag when there is no wifi match and no uploaded selfie, (c) consider Play Integrity attestation on punch (needs an app update and a native module), (d) surface a per-tech mock-day count to the owner.

findings.title: A mocked or fabricated arrive_customer punch sets the billed fuel distance
findings.claim: derive_route takes the latest arrive_customer job_location as the outbound endpoint whether or not it is mocked. Only travel samples are filtered for is_mock, and the ladder prefers the larger of path-sum and straight-line × circuity. So a mocked arrive point far from the customer inflates the fuel on the bill.
findings.failing_condition: A tech records arrive_customer with is_mock=true (or forged coordinates via the API) several km from the real pin, then submits the completion without fuel_paisa.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:124-135 — _trusted_samples drops is_mock samples only
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:101-103 — _latest_location picks the latest punch of a kind, with no is_mock filter
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:236 — arrive = _latest_location(locations, 'arrive_customer')
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:264-266 — _leg_ladder(origin, (arrive.lat, arrive.lng), samples, ...)
findings.impact: The customer is overcharged for fuel, and any fuel reimbursement to the technician is inflated. The arrive punch's MOCK/OFF-PIN badge is visible on JobDetail only if the manager opens that job.
findings.fix_sketch: In derive_route, ignore an arrive punch that is mocked or has verified=False, and fall back to the customer pin as the endpoint. Record the basis as 'pin' so the bill shows why.

findings.title: On a shared phone, the job screen shows another technician's failed outbox items and lets the current user Discard them
findings.claim: useJobOutbox filters outbox items by jobId only, and JobDetailScreen gives every failed item Retry and Discard. So tech B on a shared device can permanently delete tech A's rejected or 404-parked payments and completions for that job. The flush and attendance paths do filter by techId.
findings.failing_condition: Shared device; A's write on job J parked as failed (any definitive 4xx, including the 404 the dead Railway host returns, S9). B signs in, opens J, taps Discard.
evidence: technician-app/src/lib/outbox.ts:243-244 — itemsForJob: filter((i) => i.jobId === jobId)
technician-app/src/lib/useJobOutbox.ts:23-27 — queued/failed from itemsForJob with no techId filter
technician-app/src/features/jobs/JobDetailScreen.tsx:717-739 — every outboxView.failed item gets Discard → discardCompletionAware
technician-app/src/lib/outboxSync.ts:205 — contrast: flush skips item.techId !== me
technician-app/src/features/attendance/useAttendance.ts:99-100 — contrast: attendance failed rows filtered by tech_id
findings.impact: Breaks the outbox's 'never deletes a write without its owner's decision' contract. Cash records and completions can vanish, with no server-side trace (see O6-F15).
findings.fix_sketch: Filter itemsForJob or useJobOutbox to techId === me || techId === null, and show other technicians' items read-only with their name. Needs an app update.

findings.title: Discarding a failed punch, crossing or job write leaves no trace on the server
findings.claim: discardPunch, discardPresence and discardItem remove the record locally, with the punch selfie, and send nothing to the server. Grep finds no telemetry emitter in the technician app other than travelSync and Sentry. With production returning 404, every punch and job write is sitting in a failed list, so a technician can erase an inconvenient record and the manager never learns it existed.
findings.failing_condition: Any parked item (definitive 4xx; today every write, because the edge 404s) and the tech taps Discard.
evidence: technician-app/src/features/attendance/sync.ts:122-131 — deletes selfie file, removePunches([clientId])
technician-app/src/lib/outbox.ts:224-227 — discardItem → removeItem(id)
Grep technician-app/src for 'api/events'|'telemetry': only features/jobs/travelSync.ts and lib/sentry.ts
findings.impact: The evidence a manager would use (a late clock-in, a cash payment that bounced) can be destroyed silently. In aggregate, a technician who never clocks a late arrival looks punctual.
findings.fix_sketch: On discard, enqueue a droppable 'discarded' telemetry record (kind, client_id, job_id, failedReason, the original payload's time and amount) to POST /api/events, and surface a per-tech discard count to the manager. Or for punches, send the record with a 'withdrawn' marker instead of deleting it.

findings.title: A manager can credit their own staff ledger and approve their own advance
findings.claim: add_ledger_entry accepts any body.tech_id, including the caller's, and approve_advance never compares req.tech_id with the approving actor. Only two roles exist (tech, manager). So a manager can write an earning or adjustment_credit to themselves or a favoured tech and then disburse against it, with no second person involved.
findings.failing_condition: Manager m1 POSTs /api/attendance/ledger {tech_id: 'm1', kind: 'earning', ...}, or approves an advance_request whose tech_id is m1 (once the advance policy is switched on).
evidence: backend/app/features/attendance/router.py:463-470 — add_ledger_entry(body=body, actor=principal.tech_id) with no tech_id vs actor check
backend/app/features/attendance/schemas.py:513-519 — LedgerEntryRequest.tech_id free
backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:1301-1309 — StaffLedger(tech_id=body.tech_id, recorded_by=actor)
backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:1629-1644 — approve_advance: no req.tech_id != actor check
findings.impact: Wage money moves on one person's say-so. The chain records recorded_by, but nothing flags self-dealing and nobody runs verify (O6-F07).
findings.fix_sketch: Refuse rows where body.tech_id == actor and self-approval of advances. Add an 'owner' role (or an owner-review queue) for manager-on-manager money, and a daily digest to the owner of all ledger writes and voids.

findings.title: The ops console login is a shared password with no attempt throttling
findings.claim: ops-server.mjs checks a single OPS_PASSWORD on POST /api/ops/login with no attempt counter or delay. So once the ops hostname is published through the tunnel without Cloudflare Access, it can be brute-forced at line rate, and it holds the platform and Sentry tokens and the backend proxy token.
findings.failing_condition: Ops hostname in the tunnel ingress without an Access policy, and a guessable OPS_PASSWORD.

result.design:
AUDIT/FORENSICS MINIMUM (what must exist before the pakka-khata flows to Odoo)
1. Void metadata on every voidable money row. job_payment gains voided_by/voided_at (staff_ledger already has them, models.py:479-482). Every void writes a job_event whose payload is {payment_id, amount_paisa, method, reason}, so a void can be tied to its row. Payment-create events carry the same payload (today they carry only text: service.py:1478-1484).
2. Bill snapshot history. Add an append-only job_bill_revision table (job_id, rev, kind completion|override|negotiate|send, original_paisa, negotiated_paisa, materials JSONB, labour_rate, time_spent, fuel_paisa/basis, actor, reason, created_at), written in the same transaction as every completion upsert, negotiate and bill send. This stops clear_materials (service.py:1225) and the bill_original_paisa overwrite from destroying evidence. A manager override and a post-send negotiate require a reason.
3. Append-only approval records. A single approval table (subject_type: advance|bill_override|negotiate_over_cap|erp_batch|ledger_entry, subject_id, decision, decided_by from the principal never the body, decided_at, reason). Self-approval is refused (decided_by != subject tech, or != recorded_by). Rejections are never deleted. This is also the shape the Odoo supervised transfer (S-04 F35) needs: Odoo receives only rows with an 'approved' decision, and the export batch carries its approval id.
4. Actor from the principal everywhere. Fix attendance_adjustment.manager_id (O6-F10) and audit other body-supplied actor fields.
5. One tamper-evident money chain. Generalise attendance/chain.py into a per-shop chain covering staff_ledger, job_payment create/void and job_bill_revision. Verify daily on the scheduler, write the result to app_event, and push the head_hash to the owner out of band (WhatsApp/email) or to a locked object under a different account. That anchor is the only thing that defeats an operator who can recompute an unkeyed chain.
6. Client-side destruction becomes visible. A discard sends a droppable telemetry record. A per-tech count of discards and of mock or uncorroborated days appears on the manager board and in the owner digest.
7. DB-enforced append-only. With the role split (O6-F18), REVOKE UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on job_event, staff_ledger_chain, attendance_event, attendance_adjustment, shop_setting and job_bill_revision from the runtime role, and grant column-level UPDATE only on void columns. Code conventions then become DB facts.
8. An owner role, or at minimum an owner-only read-only digest, so that manager-on-manager money (O6-F16) has a second pair of eyes. Today there are only tech and manager.

HOME-BOX OPERATOR MODEL
Threat actors: (a) internet scanners hitting tunnel hostnames; (b) a technician with a valid PIN/JWT; (c) a manager; (d) the operator, the person with a shell on the box, who may not be the owner; (e) anyone who walks off with the box or its disk; (f) Cloudflare as TLS terminator.
What the tunnel changes: no inbound port is needed (R-03 F1/F2), but every hostname in the ingress is public, and the tunnel token itself lets any holder run a connector for that tunnel. That is from my own knowledge and was not fetched in W1, so verify it. The tunnel token is therefore a top-tier secret. It does not remove LAN exposure: Docker-published ports bypass ufw (R-03 F16), and docker-group membership or a mounted docker.sock is root on the host (R-03 F17).
Network layout:
- Postgres, the backup job and any admin UI have no published ports (or bind to 127.0.0.1) on an internal Docker network.
- cloudflared is the only egress-to-edge path.
- Ingress has three hostnames: api.<domain> (open; the phones need it; rate-limited at Cloudflare), manager.<domain> and ops.<domain> (both behind Cloudflare Access with owner/manager email OTP; Free plan up to 50 users per R-03 F4, to be verified).
- Do not mount docker.sock into any container (Uptime Kuma, watchtower and the like).
- SSH is key-only, and admin happens over a tailnet or LAN rather than a published hostname.
Boot safety: the backend must fail closed on DEV_JWT_SECRET regardless of Railway detection (O6-F01). Rotate all seeded PINs before the tunnel goes up (O6-F05). Disable /docs in production (O6-F19).
Secrets at rest: one env file today grants JWT forgery, R2 read/write/delete and WhatsApp/FCM sending (config.py:35-36,133-140,151). Move secrets to root-only 0600 files or Docker secrets, keep them out of any backup of the box, and split them by process: the API never needs the backup-encryption private key or the tunnel token.
Database: use least-privilege roles (O6-F18). Keep fsync and full_page_writes on, and put the box on a UPS because Karachi load-shedding makes power loss routine (R-03 F15). The local superuser password is not kept on the box in plaintext.
Backups: encrypt with age to the owner's offline key; ship to a separate bucket or account with a put-only token and provider-side retention or lock; copy a second set off-box. The operator can read or edit live data but cannot silently delete or alter history once it has left the box. Monthly restore drills (RUNBOOK-BACKUPS.md) also verify the chain anchor against the restored head.
Who can read staff_ledger: through the API, any manager for any tech (router.py:515-526) and each tech for themselves (/ledger/me). Through the DB, the single app role, any dump holder and the operator. After the redesign: managers and the owner through the API; fixflow_app and fixflow_backup in the DB; dumps readable only with the owner's key.
Residual risk to accept explicitly: an operator with root on the live box can still alter live rows. The design does not stop that. It makes the alteration detectable within a day through the out-of-band head-hash anchor and the encrypted, put-only backups.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the path myself and the failing condition holds. config.py:160 defaults `environment` to "dev". config.py:221 sets `is_production` true only when environment=="production" or RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT is present. config.py:228 makes the boot guard (called first thing in create_app, main.py:251) raise only when is_production is true AND jwt_secret == DEV_JWT_SECRET. On a self-hosted box with neither variable set, is_production is False, the guard does nothing, and jwt_secret keeps its default from config.py:151, which is the constant committed at config.py:17. security.py:62/67 then signs and verifies HS256 tokens with that public string.

Forging a manager token works in practice. In identity/deps.py:42-60, get_current_principal decodes the token, loads the row by `sub`, and checks only `active` and `ver == token_version`. The role comes from the DB row, so an attacker needs a manager id and its token_version. Migration 0012 seeds the manager id 'm1' in the public repo (tech ids are slugs t1..t5, per models.py:3). A missing `ver` claim counts as 0, the column default, and it is a small integer anyone can guess if it was ever bumped. So {sub:'m1', exp:...} signed with the dev secret gives a manager principal.

Nothing else blocks this. backend/Dockerfile and start.sh never set FIXFLOW_ENVIRONMENT, docker-compose.yml does not either, and backend/.env.example has no FIXFLOW_ENVIRONMENT line, so an operator copying it gets no prompt to set one. ops/health.py:121 reports 'degraded' only when is_production is true, so the deep-health check stays silent in this case too. Commits since 906b990: da988e2 changed config.py only in the database_url validator, and none of the listed commits touch the guard.

Adjacent issue I noticed but did not run: .env.example ships `FIXFLOW_JWT_SECRET=` blank. pydantic-settings does not ignore empty env values by default (no env_ignore_empty in model_config), so a .env copied verbatim would make jwt_secret "". That differs from DEV_JWT_SECRET, so the guard would pass even WITH FIXFLOW_ENVIRONMENT=production.

Why P1 and not P0: if the condition occurs, the impact is full auth bypass (P0-class). But the self-hosted deploy does not exist yet (the docs/ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md and G1 gate describe it as planned), and the bug needs an operator to leave the variable out. The fix is cheap: fail closed when not explicitly 'dev', or reject any secret shorter than N bytes or equal to the default, regardless of environment.
verdicts.what_would_settle_it: Run in backend/ with RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT and FIXFLOW_ENVIRONMENT unset and no FIXFLOW_JWT_SECRET: `python -c "from app.main import create_app; create_app(); from app.core.config import settings, DEV_JWT_SECRET; print(settings.is_production, settings.jwt_secret == DEV_JWT_SECRET)"`. Expect it to boot and print `False True`. Then sign a token with `jwt.encode({'sub':'m1','exp':<future>}, DEV_JWT_SECRET, 'HS256')` and call a CurrentManager endpoint against a migrated DB. Expect 200.

verdicts.reasoning: I traced the path myself. router.py:308-335: POST /jobs/{job_id}/bill/negotiate takes `principal: CurrentPrincipal` and has no `dependencies=[Depends(require_manager)]`, while other routes in the same file do have it (lines 111, 128, 233, 369, 450). The router is mounted with a plain `app.include_router(jobs_router, prefix="/api")` (main.py:300), so no router-level role gate is added. identity/deps.py:64 shows CurrentPrincipal accepts any valid token of any role. service.py:1381-1402: negotiate_bill loads the row with `_load`, which only checks that the job exists and shop_id matches (service.py:1910-1914), with no assignment scoping. The only guards are `status == "closed"` (409) and `bill_original_paisa is None` (400). After those it sets bill_negotiated_paisa = amount_paisa and bill_status = "negotiated" unconditionally. It never reads assigned_tech_id, bill_sent_at, payments, or the original amount. schemas.py:145-147: NegotiateRequest.amount_paisa is `Field(..., ge=0)`, so 0 is accepted and there is no bound relative to the original. Compare the customer-pin action at service.py:1612, which has `if not actor_is_manager and row.assigned_tech_id != actor: raise JobForbiddenError`; negotiate has no equivalent check. The negotiated figure really does change what the customer owes: _detail (service.py:1955-1962) uses bill_negotiated_paisa as `payable` when it is set, so balance_paisa = payable - received. Setting it to 0 after a payment leaves a zero or negative balance. The bill freeze (bill_sent_at, negotiated, or non-voided payment) only guards completion resubmits; log_customer_message's own comment (service.py:1427-1431) says so. No notification is raised; the call only adds a `bill` timeline event. The uncommitted working-tree diff only touches tech_metrics, and no commit since 906b990 in gitLog.txt changes negotiate_bill. So the failing condition holds: a tech JWT can POST {amount_paisa: 0} to any non-closed job that has a bill, whoever it is assigned to, whether or not the bill was sent or paid. Why I rated it P2 rather than P1: (1) tech access to negotiate is intended. The mobile app's outbox has a "negotiate" kind (technician-app/src/lib/outbox.ts:28, JobDetailScreen.tsx:89) because haggling happens on site, often after the customer has seen the bill. So the real gaps are the missing assigned-tech check and the missing freeze once a payment exists, not tech access as such. (2) It needs an authenticated staff member, so it is an insider risk. (3) Every renegotiation is logged with actor=principal.tech_id and the prior and new amounts in the event text, so it can be detected after the fact. There is no approval step or real-time alert, though.

verdicts.corrected_claim: The mechanics are as claimed. The confidentiality impact is mostly not new, though: the same env that holds the R2 key also holds FIXFLOW_DATABASE_URL, which gives live read/write on the DB. The real gap is availability and integrity. Whoever can wipe the DB with that env can also delete every backup with the same R2 key, so the backups do not survive the compromise they most need to survive. "Plaintext" means no application-level encryption. R2's provider-side at-rest encryption does nothing against someone holding the key.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the path myself. run_db_backup takes the default get_storage() R2Storage, which is the single boto3 client keyed with settings.r2_access_key_id/secret and bound to settings.r2_bucket (default and documented prod value: job-media). The dump bytes from pg_dump go to put_object unmodified, with no application-level encryption. The same client then lists the backups/db/ prefix and calls delete_object on stale keys. A credential that can PUT, LIST and DELETE in that bucket can therefore read and delete every dump, and the code has no line that narrows the credential, the bucket or the delete scope. The runbook confirms the shared bucket and shared credential in prod and lists them as an open known limit, so the claim holds.

I lowered the severity from P1 to P2 for three reasons:
(1) The failing condition needs the backend env or code execution in the API. That same env carries DATABASE_URL, so reading the dumps adds little beyond direct DB access. The incremental harm is the attacker destroying both the DB and every backup, a total-loss scenario for a single-tenant shop.
(2) The "buggy prune" path is bounded in the current code. keys_to_prune only deletes keys matching fixflow-db-<stamp>.dump under the prefix that are older than retention_days, so a bug would need a code change.
(3) Bucket-side controls such as an R2 bucket lock, versioning or a scoped token cannot be seen from the repo and might mitigate deletion. Nothing in the repo or runbook says they exist, so I did not count them.
verdicts.what_would_settle_it:
Two account-side checks would settle the severity:
- Cloudflare R2 bucket job-media: look for a bucket-lock / retention rule on backups/db/ and check whether versioning is on. A lock would block deletion inside the retention window.
- R2 API token behind FIXFLOW_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID: check whether it is scoped to Object Read & Write on job-media (it can delete) or is narrower.

A practical test: with the prod token, run `railway run python -c "from app.core.storage import get_storage; s=get_storage(); s.put_bytes('backups/db/probe.txt', b'x', 'text/plain'); s.delete('backups/db/probe.txt')"`. If the delete succeeds, the deletion path is live.
